aux_label: \newlabel{lemma-pointwise-envelope-degree-two-boundary}{{12.8}{26}{The degree-two boundary of a pointwise envelope}{subsection.12.8}{}}

checks: The P-actions on F, A=Pi(F), and F'=A/F factor through H because the kernel A acts trivially.
Twisting 0 -> F -> A -> F' -> 0 by a P-torsor is exact because the assertion is local on X.
A chosen identification of the induced H-torsor with E canonically identifies F^Q with F^E and A^Q with A^E=Pi(F^E).
The middle twist is flasque by its pointwise-envelope identification, not by the false assertion that flasqueness is local.
Flasque acyclicity over (X, Z_X) makes the H1-to-H2 connecting map an isomorphism.
A compatible isomorphism between any two P-lifts transports the twisted sequence and affine obstruction torsor; kernel ambiguity acts trivially on all coefficient twists.
The class vanishes exactly when Q reduces to G, equivalently when E is induced from a G-torsor.

Under the Stacks left-torsor convention, [E] is represented by -h_ij and d_u(Q) by +u(p_ij); the derived connecting maps send the chosen local lifts to -h_ij and -u(p_ij), so 3-by-3 anticommutativity yields the final plus sign delta(d_u(Q)).
The printed Tohoku formula partial(E)=-d(Q) is explicitly identified as the inverse transition-function convention, while the Stacks class agrees with the usual abelian connecting homomorphism.

nonclaims: No arbitrary inverse-image or topological base-change compatibility is asserted for the pointwise envelope.
No fixed target cohomology group is asserted when the H-action on F is nontrivial.
No sectionwise surjectivity is asserted for the twisted quotient A^Q -> (F')^Q.
The Stacks plus sign and the source's printed minus sign are not conflated; their transition conventions are explicitly distinguished.
